standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting projectivity along a nilpotent ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-lift-projective, invoked at proof line 2202
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that if S/JS is projective over R/J with J the radical of I, then S/IS is projective over R/I because J/I is nilpotent and S/IS is flat, contradicting the maximality of I; hence I may be taken radical.

standard_prerequisites.name: Generic flatness for a finite type algebra over a reduced Noetherian ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-generic-flatness-Noetherian (proof line 2212) and algebra-lemma-generic-flatness-reduced (proof line 2214)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a nonzero f with S_f free over R_f, which enables the faithfully flat presentation of R by R_f times its f-adic completion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Faithfully flat descent of projectivity, flatness of a completion, and the criterion for a flat pure module over a complete local ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-completion-flat (proof line 2222) and algebra-theorem-ffdescent-projectivity (proof line 2224); Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-flat-pure-over-complete-projective (proof line 2227)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces projectivity of S over R to projectivity of the completed base change, and the criterion then applies because the fibre rings stay geometrically integral and the element f lies in the Jacobson radical of the complete ring.

core_obligations: Contradict a maximal counterexample: assume the set of ideals I with S/IS not projective over R/I is nonempty and take a maximal element; with J the radical of I, if I differs from J then S/JS is projective over R/J, S/IS is flat over R/I and J/I is nilpotent, so lifting projectivity along a nilpotent ideal makes S/IS projective, a contradiction; hence I is radical and one may assume R reduced with S/IS projective over R/I for every nonzero ideal I (proof lines 2193-2207).

Introduce the faithfully flat presentation: by generic flatness there is a nonzero f with S_f free over R_f, the map R -> R_f times the f-adic completion of R is faithfully flat, so by faithfully flat descent of projectivity it suffices to show that S tensor_R R^ is projective over R^ (proof lines 2209-2225).

Apply the complete case criterion: note that S/fS is projective over R/(f) and that S tensor_R R^ is flat and of finite type over the complete ring R^; for a prime of R^ with corresponding prime of R, geometric integrality of the fibres passes to the base change, so the fibre over the residue field has a unique associated prime generated by the expansion of the prime, and that associated prime together with f does not generate the unit ideal because f lies in the Jacobson radical of the f-adically complete ring and the map on spectra is surjective since the fibres are nonempty (proof lines 2227-2243).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the radical, hence reduced, case by lifting projectivity along a nilpotent ideal (proof lines 2193-2207).
Use generic flatness and the faithfully flat presentation by the localisation and the completion to reduce to the complete case (proof lines 2209-2225).
Verify the hypotheses of the complete case criterion through geometric integrality of the fibres and the Jacobson radical argument (proof lines 2227-2243).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a flat finite type algebra S over a Noetherian ring R whose fibre rings are geometrically integral is projective as an R-module (statement lines 2178-2190, tag 05FS). The proof is a genuine contradiction argument: a maximal ideal over which projectivity fails is shown to be radical by lifting projectivity along a nilpotent ideal, generic flatness then provides a faithfully flat presentation of R by a localisation and an adic completion, and projectivity of the completed base change is checked through the criterion for flat pure modules using that the fibre associated primes are unique and that the chosen element lies in the Jacobson radical of a complete ring. The reduction to the complete case is the substance, so the claim is H2.
